introductoryTafseer: Surah Al-Ikhlas is described by the Holy Prophet as equivalent to one-third of the entire Qur'an. Mufti Muhammad Shafi explains in Ma'ariful Qur'an that the themes of the Qur'an resolve into three pillars: Tawhid (Monotheism), Risalah (Prophethood), and Akhirah (The Afterlife). This surah presents the quintessential theological definition of Tawhid, eradicating all forms of anthropomorphism, polytheism, and trinitarian philosophies.

sections.title: Absolute Oneness, As-Samad & Incomparability
sections.arabicText: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝١ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝٢ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝٣ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ ۝٤
sections.translation: Say: 'He is Allah, the [Ahad] (The Absolutely One and Indivisible). Allah, [As-Samad] (The Eternal, Self-Sufficient Refuge upon whom all depend). He neither begets nor is He begotten. And there is none comparable or equal unto Him.'

phraseCards.englishPhrase: Proclaim: He is Allah, the Single and Unique.

vocabulary.grammarNote: Ahad differs from Wahid; Ahad signifies an absolute unity that cannot be divided, multiplied, or conceived as having parts.

phraseCards.englishPhrase: Allah, the Eternal, Independent Haven for all.

vocabulary.grammarNote: The Master to whom all resort in need, who has neither internal cavity nor dependence upon sustenance.

phraseCards.englishPhrase: He neither begot any offspring, nor was He begotten of anything,

vocabulary.grammarNote: Refutation of pagans claiming angels are Allah's daughters and Christians claiming divine sonship.

phraseCards.englishPhrase: and never has there been anyone comparable or equal to Him.

vocabulary.grammarNote: Absolute transcendence over any resemblance in essence, attributes, or actions.

sections.commentary:
Mufti Shafi writes that when the polytheists of Makkah asked the Prophet: 'Trace for us the ancestry and genealogy of your Lord! Is He made of gold, silver, or iron?', Allah revealed this sublime declaration.

The divine attribute 'As-Samad' is a comprehensive reality. Ibn Abbas elucidated that it denotes the Master whose nobility is consummate, whose majesty is supreme, whose forbearance is boundless, and whose independence is absolute. Everything in the cosmos is utterly destitute before Him, while He is self-subsisting without need of food, companion, or protector.

'Lam yalid wa lam yulad' definitively rejects biological or metaphysical offspring, refuting polytheistic mythologies and trinitarian claims.

subsections.title: The Polytheists' Question on Divine Lineage
subsections.content: Narrated by Imam Ahmad, the pagans came to the Messenger of Allah demanding: 'O Muhammad, describe the nature and composition of your Lord!' This surah settled the discussion with an ontological definition of divine transcendence (Tanzih).

curatedTerms.theologicalContext: Denotes singularity without composition; unlike 'Wahid' which can head a numerical series, 'Ahad' negates any pluralization or constituent parts.

curatedTerms.literalMeaning: The solid, unshakable haven to whom everyone turns.
curatedTerms.theologicalContext: The Lord who is entirely self-sufficient, requiring neither nourishment nor progeny, while sustaining every contingent existence.
